chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hajjal, who said:

I said to Jameel ibn Darraj, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When a respectable person of a people comes to you, honor him.' He said, 'Yes.' I said to him, 'And what is the respectable one?' He said, 'I had asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, so he said that the respectable one is the one who has wealth.' I said, 'So what is the noble one?' He said: 'The one who performs good deeds with his wealth and the wealth of others.' I said, 'So what is generosity/karam?' He said: 'Piety (taqwa).'

key_terms.حَسِيب: Noble one who performs good deeds

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between being sharif, hasib, and karam in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the Shia concept of social stratification by distinguishing between material wealth (*sharif*), active benevolence (*hasib*), and spiritual piety (*karam*). It reflects the scholarly tradition of integrating Prophetic sayings with Imami interpretations to redefine nobility not merely by lineage or assets, but by the ethical application of resources and ultimate *taqwa*. This hierarchy underscores the practical implication that true honor is earned through righteous action rather than static status.
